meta.grain: county, keyed STATE|COUNTY as GS_DATA.nodes spells it; the county is resolved per bus from uni.dim_substation.fips
meta.figure_source_note: The mart's source, as_of and transaction_basis are NULL on every row: no price per acre is measured anywhere in the workspace.
meta.method: Three round dollar figures written down once and applied unchanged to every county code; no state, county or parcel differentiation is held, so none is claimed.
meta.not_a: Not an appraisal, not a quotation, not a closed-sale price and not an assessed value; those are four different numbers and this is none of them.
meta.replace_with: A county land-value series joined on fips_2020 — USDA NASS farm real-estate value per acre, the Census of Agriculture county series, the six state assessors’ parcel values, or a licensed parcel dataset with sale price and acreage.

describes.low: undeveloped rural acreage away from a load centre, with no competing use on it
describes.base: the central stand-in this product computes with until a real series lands
describes.high: acreage near a load centre, or carrying a use that has to be bought out

county_key_defects: CT FIPS codes are stored four characters wide in uni.dim_substation; they are zero-padded to join fips_2020 and the raw code is kept as fips_in_store.

VT's county name Franklin covers two codes (50011, 50012). It is one row here because the card indexes by name; the row lists both codes and the buses behind each, and would be withheld if the two carried different bands.

intensity.title: Land a project of this technology needs, per MW
intensity.source: Solar and wind carry published studies. Storage and data centres carry a trade rule of thumb, because no published study exists for either.
intensity.unit: acres per MW of project capacity
notes: This is the kill threshold for the rule-out gate, not a geometry. The search disc comes from the gen-tie length for the voltage class; this says how much of it the project needs.

area_basis says which area each row measures. The gate screens against TOTAL project area, the fenced boundary. Direct impact area is the land actually occupied and is smaller; the two differ by roughly the packing factor and confusing them decides candidates wrongly.

Solar figures rest on plants with commercial operation dates through 2019. Median power density rose roughly 45-50% between 2011 and 2019 installations, so a project built today is denser than these medians and the acreage here is conservative.
The wind band is the published mean plus or minus one standard deviation. The band shipped before 2026-09-10 ran from mean minus one sigma up to the mean, which understated every wind verdict.
Figures were read from secondary extraction of the source documents rather than from the published PDFs. Verify against the papers before any figure reaches a client.
intensity.replace_with: For storage: acres per MW derived from the plant polygons in the published utility-scale solar dataset, which covers PV-plus-battery projects and is the only route to an empirical figure. For data centres: nothing public exists.

solar.source: Bolinger and Bolinger, Land Requirements for Utility-Scale PV, IEEE Journal of Photovoltaics 12(2), 2022, for the level; Ong et al., NREL/TP-6A20-56290, 2013, for the direct-to-total ratio of about 0.82.
solar.vintage: 2022 study on plant data to 2019; ratio from 2013
solar.population: 736 plants, 27,001 MWac, commercial operation 2007-2019 across 38 states, about 92% of US utility-scale PV built in that window.
solar.note: Low is the fixed-tilt median of 3.6 ac/MWac, base the single-axis tracking median of 5.6, high the 2013 capacity-weighted total across all solar of 8.9. Tracking needs roughly 50% more land per MW than fixed tilt.

wind.source: Denholm et al., Land-Use Requirements of Modern Wind Power Plants in the United States, NREL/TP-6A2-45834, 2009.
wind.population: 172 projects above 20 MW built after 2000, more than 26 GW; the direct-impact subset is 93 projects and about 14 GW.
wind.note: Total project area is 85 plus or minus 55 acres/MW, so the band is the mean plus or minus one sigma. Direct impact is 0.74 acres/MW permanent, 2.5 including temporary disturbance. Rotors have grown and spacing widened since 2009, so treat the mean as a floor rather than a centre.

bess.source: Industry rule of thumb. No published study on storage land-use intensity exists; every available figure is vendor or brokerage material.
bess.note: Four-hour duration. Longer duration raises this roughly in proportion. This row must never render as though a study stands behind it.

hybrid.source: Industry rule of thumb: the cited solar figures plus the uncited storage ones, sharing one point of interconnection. The storage half is uncited, so the sum is uncited.
hybrid.note: Solar plus co-located storage. Inherits the storage row lack of a source.

dc.source: Industry rule of thumb. No published study exists; the only quantitative anchors are brokerage research behind a paywall.
dc.note: Building plus yard and substation. The denominator is unresolved: campus figures in trade sources are denominated on IT load while this product works in interconnection MW, and the two differ materially.
